general.title: What these estimates cannot tell you

items.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
The baseline repeats recent permit trends under today's rules. It does not predict a recession or a boom.
Counties without a permit office, or with imputed permit counts, carry the Census Bureau's estimates.
For-sale townhouses and condominiums: every new building is valued as a rental.
Which lots sit side by side, or which owners would sell.
The real price of a house bought to be torn down; census home values are owners' own estimates.
Local zoning detail: the share of lots zoned for one home only is a statewide range.
Lending and building-code rules for the larger buildings in this range.

title.text: How many more homes would Pennsylvania permit?

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms
Baseline: homes permitted under today's rules

body.text: Over 2027–2031, Pennsylvania would likely permit between 95 and 1,500 more homes (0.069–1.3%) with two to six homes allowed on single-family lots, on top of a baseline of 67,000–180,000 homes expected under today's rules.

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

body.text: Decision support, not a forecast. Not an official state document.

Housing Data and Technology Innovation Challenge, Participant Handbook, "Benchmark Policy Scenarios" and "The five scenarios"

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

label.text: More homes permitted, this reform alone
Eligible single-family lots in single-family-only zones

meaning.text: Single-family lots in zones that allow only one home today.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of eligible lots = max(census single-family homes x lot-count correction x single-family-only zoned share - ADU overlap share x lots used by ADUs, 0) = 1,873,911 lots, 2,180,643 lots, 2,455,296 lots

label.text: Lots large enough for a 2-6 unit building

cites.value: lots large enough for a 2-6 unit building (missing_middle: sf_detached)
cites.shown: Lots large enough for a 2-6 unit building

meaning.text: Of those, lots big enough for a small apartment building or townhouses.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots large enough = eligible lots x f, where f is the measured share, else the share of homes whose block land per home x lot share is at least the smallest lot for a 2-6 unit building, else the ledger fit share = 1,501,556 lots, 1,760,709 lots, 2,010,356 lots

meaning.text: Of those, lots where a new small building would be worth more than the house and the cost of building it.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of feasible lots = lots large enough x sum over k = 2..6 of mix weight w_k x p_k, where p_k = share of the tract's owner home values at or below residual land value of a k-unit building / (1 + acquisition premium) = 3,582 lots, 14,493 lots, 40,164 lots

cites.value: lots redeveloped 2027-2031 (missing_middle: sf_detached)

meaning.text: Of those, the ones expected to be rebuilt over the five years.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots redeveloped = feasible lots x min(yearly hazard h, yearly turnover) x sum over 2027-2031 of ramp(t) = 33.69 lots, 165.9 lots, 582.73 lots

cites.value: new units in 2-6 unit buildings 2027-2031 (missing_middle: sf_detached)

meaning.text: Homes in the new buildings on those lots.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of new units = sum over k of lots redeveloped with k-unit buildings x k = 148.41 units, 692.48 units, 2,383 units

cites.value: net new units after demolition 2027-2031 (missing_middle: sf_detached)

meaning.text: New homes minus the houses torn down to make room.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of net units = new units - lots redeveloped x homes demolished per lot (1) = 114.48 units, 529.47 units, 1,802 units

cites.value: net added units 2027-2031 (missing_middle: sf_detached)

meaning.text: What is left after taking out homes that would have been built anyway: the reform's own addition.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of net added units = net units x (1 - displacement share x) = 94.59 units, 439.62 units, 1,484 units

body.text: Middle estimate: 0.35% more homes than the baseline. “Little effect” means under 1%.
Single-family lots in zones that allow only one home today.

body.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
Decision support, not a forecast. Not an official state document.
